title: The Siege of Madinah & The Trial of Faith
subtitle: Treachery on the Flank: Banu Qurayza and the Trembling Hearts
summary: The confederates before the trench in the classical sirah, Ali's duel with Amr as that biography tells it, the break with Banu Qurayzah as the sirah tells it, and the Quran's description of that hour in Surah al-Ahzab.

sections.text: The Arrival of the Confederate Armies

The classical sirah places the Quraysh and their allies on one side of the trench and Ghatafan on the other, and it gives the familiar totals of about four thousand and about six thousand, together about ten thousand. Those counts are not a verse and they are not a Hadith number cited here. The Quran says that the believers were shaken and that armies came at them. It does not state the total.

For nearly a month, the two forces confronted each other across the divide. The Muslim garrison of three thousand men stood stationed along the southern embankment, their backs to Mount Sal'. Day and night, enemy archers rained arrows across the ditch, attempting to force a passage. Skirmishes erupted whenever confederate cavalry rode along the rim seeking narrow gaps.
The Breach at the Ditch & The Duel of Ali

A daring group of Makkan equestrian champions, led by the veteran warrior Amr ibn Abd Wudd alongside Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl and Dirar ibn al-Khattab, spurred their chargers over a narrow section of the trench, landing on the Madinan side. Amr, an eighty-year-old warrior celebrated across the peninsula as being equal to a thousand fighters, rode forward insolently in full chain armor, demanding a champion for single combat: 'Who among you dares to duel me?'

Ali ibn Abi Talib immediately stepped forward, asking the Prophet's permission. The Prophet ﷺ cautioned him: 'It is Amr!' Ali replied: 'Even if it is Amr!' Ali walked out to meet the armored veteran on foot. In a brief and legendary clash of swords, Ali parried Amr's fierce downward strike with his shield, which was cleaved in two, and struck him across the leg with a fatal blow. As the dust cleared, the cry of 'Allahu Akbar!' thundered from the Muslim lines. Panicked by the death of their champion, Ikrimah and the remaining riders scrambled desperately back across the ditch.

While the northern perimeter held firm, an existential catastrophe developed in the rear. Huyayy ibn Akhtab, chief of Banu al-Nadir, slipped under cover of darkness to the southern fortresses of Banu Qurayza, the last remaining Jewish tribe bound by mutual defense treaties with the Muslims. Huyayy knocked on the gate of Ka'b ibn Asad, chief of Qurayza. Ka'b initially refused to open, stating: 'Woe to you, Huyayy! Muhammad has never been anything but faithful and honorable to our treaty.'

The sirah says Huyayy ibn Akhtab pressed Ka'b ibn Asad until Banu Qurayzah set aside the pact, and that Huyayy spoke of the size of the confederate camp and of staying until Muhammad was finished. That speech is the biography's account. It is not quoted here as a Hadith. Madinah then had the confederates beyond the trench and Banu Qurayzah on the other side of the town, where women and children had been gathered in the strongholds. The sirah does not turn that danger into a claim that every Muslim was about to be killed.

When verification of Qurayza's betrayal reached the Prophet ﷺ via Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and Sa'd ibn Ubadah, the psychological pressure reached an agonizing zenith. The Qur'an immortalized that terrifying hour in Surah Al-Ahzab:

إِذْ جَاءُوكُم مِّن فَوْقِكُمْ وَمِنْ أَسْفَلَ مِنكُمْ وَإِذْ زَاغَتِ الْأَبْصَارُ وَبَلَغَتِ الْقُلُوبُ الْحَنَاجِرَ وَتَظُنُّونَ بِاللَّهِ الظُّنُونَا ۚ هُنَالِكَ ابْتُلِيَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَزُلْزِلُوا زِلْزَالًا شَدِيدًا
'When they came at you from above you and from below you, and when eyes shifted in fear, and hearts reached the throats, and you assumed about Allah diverse doubts. There the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking.' (Surah Al-Ahzab 33:10–11)

Hypocrites began deserting the front, claiming their domestic homes were exposed, while true believers stood shoulder to shoulder in the freezing darkness, their reliance upon Allah unwavering in the face of apparent annihilation.

references.title: The Holy Quran
references.author: Surah Al-Ahzab (33:10–25)
references.notes: Divine description of the severe trial, the betrayal on the flank, and the differing reactions of believers and hypocrites.

references.title: Sahih al-Bukhari
references.author: Imam Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari (d. 256 AH)
references.notes: Aishah: the verse 'when they came at you from above you and from below you' (33:10) was the day of the trench. The duel with Amr and the troop totals are Ibn Hisham, not this Hadith. Bukhari 4110, the later statement about going out to them, is cited in the next chapter.
